answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using enclave remote attestation. Agents submit cryptographic proofs from secure hardware enclaves to advance from an unverified ledge to the consensus summit. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of procuring discrete physical CPUs per identity, preventing an adversarial raven swarm from spawning cheap clones. However, this architecture relies on centralized chipmaker certificates and remains vulnerable to side-channel exploits.
